
== Trim and crossover players, 13 October 2026 ==
* Per Bill: product detail is kept to set names only. The per-set sections, the table and the card counts were removed, so the earlier notes on counts and products no longer apply.
* 2001 World Championship: still no archived source, so it stays out of the article.
* Player matching uses the small-world rule: an exact full name, plus membership in the Decipher volunteer community (Squadron or SWCCG events), plus attendance at DecipherCon 1999, is treated as the same person. Results come from Decipher's DecipherCon 1999 event-score pages.
* Left out as ambiguous: Phil Pipitone (not clearly the modern player of that name), Nick Steiner, and Jason Winter (a Decipherian).
* Greg Heisler and Ian Vincent (YJ world champions in 1999 and 2000) have no wiki person page, so they're named only in Organized play. [[User:Datacard Grok|Datacard Grok]] ([[User talk:Datacard Grok|talk]]) 18:10, 13 October 2026 (UTC)

=== Possibly faulty data ===
* 2003 Young Jedi World Championship entry fee: the Players Committee's Gen Con page (28 May 2003) gives $5; a player who chose not to enter wrote on 30 July 2003 that it was $8 (post 31121). Both are cited.
=== Marginal cuts ===
* Players' opinions on dueling decks (primogen, January 2003 and August 2005), the Coruscant Guard/Destroyer Droid "killed the game" view, and the description of Reflections' Combo Battle Cards and Dual Cards (product detail is kept to set names; a Decipher source would be the primary source).
* Bubba Joe's remark that Young Jedi was getting a third virtual card set (unconfirmed); John Keahey's online player list (identity of PloKeahey not stated in the post).
=== Missing data ===
* Places 2–6 of the 2003 Young Jedi World Championship were asked for (post 31419) but not posted in this topic.

== Old PC website (swccgpc.com) facts added, 24 November 2026 ==
Added from Players Committee forum posts (refs pcf-…, each with its Internet Archive copy): Decipher's ''Young Jedi Reflections'' facts (as quoted on the forum by Artie Deco from a saved Decipher page), [[Jim Colson]] on the FP1/FP2 promotional foils and the Japanese/German printings, primogen's comments (2003, 2005), 2004 Worlds attendance ([[Brandon Schele]]), the [[2005 Young Jedi World Championship]], the empty free sealed event at the 2005 Oklahoma States, [[Glenn Hall]]'s later Beaverton events, [[David Kangas]] (Shadow 31) on the Portland crowd, the January 2003 online tournament proposal and the 5-per-color rule.
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Colson's promo-foil post gives its years with question marks ("DecipherCon 1999?", "(1999?)", "(2002?)"); the article keeps only "in 1999, as he recalled" and drops the other years.
* 2004 Worlds attendance is Schele's estimate ("I believe", "I think").
* The 2005 Young Jedi Worlds field size is not stated anywhere: the "two dudes" remark is by a poster who had never played, and the "fifty percent" remark is a joke implying two players. Both are quoted with attribution, not written as a count.
* "Booker", who posted that he finished 2nd, is taken to be [[James Booker]] (small-world rule: same Ohio circle, Tim Simon calls James Booker "Runner-Up Champion" in the same period).
=== Left out ===
* PloKeahey's real name: he signs "--John" and his homepage path is keahey/John, which points to John Keahey, but neither the post nor the wiki states the full name; left as the handle. His player list URL (homepage.mac.com) left out (uncaptured).
* primogen's location (Minnesota): only inferable from his e-mail domain; left out. primogen's "Virtual Obi from the first set" remark is not in post 10424.
